taxonomic_note: Accepted species; Kew gives a native range from Texas to northeastern Mexico.
look_here_first: Start with one mature complete leaf: this is a BIFOLIOLATE (one-pair) herbaceous PERENNIAL, not an annual. Both leaflets are relatively broad (roughly 1.3–1.8× as long as wide), hairy and often gray-toned. Magnify stem hairs for a mix of short backward-pointing hairs, tiny glandlike hairs and stiff longer setae, then confirm sepals, floral anthers and erect hairy mature pods; compare carefully against S. roemeriana and S. bauhinioides.

best_field_traits: herbaceous perennial (2024 peer-reviewed taxonomic flora; corrected from older annual shortcut)
exactly one leaflet pair per compound leaf
leaflets relatively broad, about 1.3–1.8 times as long as wide
mixture of short retrorse hairs, glandlike trichomes and longer stiff setae on stems
extrafloral gland at the point where the paired leaflets join
persistent sepals on developing fruit; anthers constricted below symmetric terminal pollen pore
erect oblong pods roughly 2–4 cm long, hairy/setose; can persist after opening
morphology_keys.comparison_training: S. roemeriana is also perennial and has one leaflet pair, but its leaflets are much more narrowly lanceolate (approximately 2–9 times as long as wide). S. bauhinioides also has a single broad pair; distinguish with stiff mixed stem hairs, persistent sepals, anther/pod detail, and S. bauhinioides stout thickened style + rough seed testa. Life history, leaflet count alone and yellow flowers do not separate this trio.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Broad paired leaflets + retrorse hairs and stiff setae versus narrow paired leaflets in S. roemeriana; against S. bauhinioides, use floral style/anther and mature pod/seed plus indumentum; retain uncertain ID if no reproductive material.

diagnostic_image_needs: whole herbaceous perennial habit with scale
ONE entire mature compound leaf showing exactly two broad leaflets
sharp true-macro of the three kinds of stem hairs and the leaf junction gland
flower closeup with stamens and persistent sepals
erect mature hairy pod and opening valves
side-by-side S. roemeriana narrow paired leaves and S. bauhinioides broad paired leaves at the same scale
